explanation: Only III is guaranteed by the inverse function theorem. I is not guaranteed because f is discontinuous at x=-3. II fails because f(-2)=2 and f'(-2)=0; a differentiable inverse there would contradict the chain rule. At x=0, f is continuously differentiable, f(0)=4, and f'(0)≠0, so the local inverse satisfies (f⁻¹)'(4)=1/f'(0).
